## 1. SURFACE

Two-col ASCII, tab-sep, decimal-comma (EU locale): `47183,554644\t19261,547207`. Col1 = x-axis, monotonic descending (47183→1648). Context ("Raman Setup", graphene, G/2D fit) implies col1 = Raman shift in cm⁻¹, col2 = intensity (counts).

## 2. CONTENT

Range check: col1 spans 1648.7 → 47183.6. Canonical graphene lines: D≈1350, G≈1582, 2D≈2680 cm⁻¹. Real Raman spectra rarely exceed ~3500 cm⁻¹. Max here is 47183 — **13x** too big. Min (1648.7) already sits *above* canonical G (1582) — G peak position not even inside range if axis read as literal cm⁻¹.

Decision table — candidate transforms, mechanical peaks x1=19139.420 (dominant, prom=67146.6), x2=3745.339 (prom=10727.6), tested vs canonical lines:

| Transform | Fit param (from x1) | Predicted x2-mapped value | Canonical target | Land on line? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Identity | — | x1=19139.4, x2=3745.3 | G=1582, 2D=2680 | NO — both way off |
| Linear k·x (x1→G) | k=0.08266 | k·x2=309.6 | 2D=2680 | NO |
| Linear k·x (x1→2D) | k=0.14107 | k·x2=528.4 | G=1582 | NO |
| Offset r−x (x1→G) | r=20721.4 | r−x2=16976.1 | 2D=2680 | NO |
| Offset r−x (x1→2D) | r=21839.4 | r−x2=18094.1 | G=1582 | NO |
| Reciprocal k/x (x1→G) | k=3.028e7 | k/x2=8084.3 | 2D=2680 | NO |
| Reciprocal k/x (x1→2D) | k=5.168e7 | k/x2=13797.5 | G=1582 | NO |

Zero transforms land both peaks on canonical lines simultaneously. Falsifies "col1 = calibrated Raman shift cm⁻¹."

Also tested: absolute-wavenumber-minus-laser hypothesis (x1 ≈ Rayleigh/laser line, common lasers 488/514.5/532/633/785nm) — 514.5nm gives nu_laser=19436.3, only 297 off x1=19139.4 (~1.5%). Suggestive x1 = laser-line leakage/notch artifact, not a phonon peak at all — its huge dominance (amplitude 79367 vs 12554, near CCD top-5 saturation cluster at x≈19044–19332) fits laser-line/detector-saturation signature better than a Raman G/2D bump.

**CONTENT VERDICT: MISMATCH**

## 3. MISREADINGS

- **Misread: parse col1 as literal Raman shift cm⁻¹, fit G at biggest peak (x1=19139), 2D at second peak (x2=3745).** Evidence against: range 15x too big for known G/2D window; no transform (identity/linear/offset/reciprocal) puts both x1,x2 on 1582/2680 simultaneously (table above). Real G–2D gap ≈1100 cm⁻¹; here gap =15394 (14x too wide), ratio x1/x2=5.11 vs true G/2D ratio 0.59 — falsified.
- **Misread: decimal-comma treated as CSV thousands-separator or field delimiter.** `47183,554644` naive-split on comma → garbage columns (4 fields instead of 2, or truncates to int 47183). Mechanical stats note "commas normalized" — confirms this trap exists and was avoided; a naive `pd.read_csv` without `decimal=','` would silently corrupt every row.
- **Misread: assume col1 ascending (standard for most spectral tools/interpolators).** Data is monotonic_descending=True. Peak finder had to explicitly re-sort ascending — a fitter that assumes ascending x without checking will get flipped/garbage curve shape or negative dx in gradient-based fits.
- **Misread: x1 (dominant, prom=67146.6) = a real phonon peak (G or 2D).** Survives partial support (close-ish to 514.5nm laser wavenumber, off 1.5%) but amplitude/prominence profile (near CCD saturation cluster, ~6x taller than x2) matches laser-line leakage/Rayleigh artifact convention better than a Raman peak — world knowledge: G/2D are broad moderate bumps, not the tallest spike near an instrument's fixed reference line.
- **Surviving hypothesis:** col1 units uncalibrated/non-standard (possibly raw grating/pixel-to-wavenumber axis before proper Raman-shift conversion, or absolute wavenumber not shift-from-laser) — none of the 4 canonical families explain both peaks together, and neither peak's magnitude nor spacing matches G/2D physics. Task's "fit G and 2D peak" cannot be trusted to mean "top-2 mechanical peaks" without recalibrating x-axis to true Raman shift first.

CONTENT VERDICT: MISMATCH
